clue.text: Opening plan

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small door or opening in a ship's deck or a wall
second meaning: to devise a scheme

explanation.surface: An architect's opening plan for a building, or the first move in a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a deck aperture and a verb for devising a scheme in secret.

clue.text: Something else, stolen goods?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone or something exceptional
second meaning: hot is slang for stolen, and stuff is goods

explanation.walkthrough: 'Something else' is an idiom for remarkable; hot as slang for stolen is common in crime talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes an impressive or exciting person or thing, and also loot recently taken by thieves.

clue.text: Is this writer fired up about British capital?

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: taken as written
the setter refers to themself
set alight
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A writer wonders whether they are excited about the British capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British capital' looks like London, but British is just B and the capital stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tbilisi is the capital city of Georgia, in the Caucasus, so it is an example of a national capital.

clue.text: Head sliced off, jiggle fish

indicators.note: having its head cut off means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to jiggle is to shake

explanation.surface: A fishmonger decapitates a fish and gives it a wobble.
explanation.definitionFit: Hake is a white-fleshed sea fish related to cod, so it is an example of the general category.

clue.text: Rotten crack in ball

parts.note: food that is rotten has gone off
a crack is a break

explanation.surface: A rotten ball has split open along a crack.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an off break is a delivery from a spin bowler that turns into a right-handed batter from the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket delivery is called a ball, and this is one particular type of spinning delivery.

clue.text: I'd find a girl, out to save boy, modest

indicators.note: saving something means keeping it safely held, so one piece goes inside the other
out can mean disordered or wrong, so the preceding letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: letters to rearrange, taken as written
Tom is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A man hopes to find a partner who is unassuming and will rescue a young lad.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means moderately good, middling or so-so, which matches modest in the sense of unremarkable.

clue.text: Mentioned what Cupid has for lover

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so we want a word with the same sound as the phrase that follows

parts.note: Cupid carries a bow and arrows

explanation.surface: Cupid has a weapon for making people fall in love.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is an old-fashioned word for a boyfriend or male admirer, so it means a lover or sweetheart.

clue.text: Moving one book up, only covers seen on volume

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
a tome is a large book

indicators.note: the covers of a word are its outside letters, and only those are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Shifting a book up the shelf, a reader sees only the covers on the volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' looks like part of the action of shifting books, but it is the definition, in the sense of touching.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moving stirs strong feelings, and emotive likewise describes what arouses emotion.

clue.text: Work requirement, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: judging by the sound means we want a word spoken the same as the preceding idea

parts.note: a requirement is a need

explanation.surface: A job requirement that only sounds like one.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead dough is to work it with the hands, pressing and folding until it is smooth.

clue.text: Fashionable, irrational surrealist painters acting as if related

parts.note: fashionable things are in

indicators.note: surrealist art distorts reality, so the following letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy
letters to rearrange, taken as written

explanation.surface: Trendy, wild surrealist artists behave as though they belong to one family.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase means in the place of a parent, used of teachers and guardians.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in this position takes on a parent's responsibilities without being the parent, acting as though a family member.

clue.text: Get more involved in refitting of kitchen

indicators.note: refitting a room means rebuilding it in a new layout, so the word that follows is rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a bigger role in a kitchen renovation.
explanation.definitionFit: When a plot thickens it becomes more complicated and tangled, so to thicken is to grow more intricate.

clue.text: Up the creek, where fox lives?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, taken literally: a fox makes its den in a burrow in the ground

explanation.walkthrough: Up the creek is an idiom for being in difficulty; the question mark flags the literal reading of the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stuck in a pit is the stock idiom for trouble, and a fox's earth is literally a burrow dug in the ground.

clue.text: Spare hydrogen in container

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the first is placed inside the second

parts.note: a tin is a metal container
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A spare canister of hydrogen gas kept in storage.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare, lean person or frame is slender, so the adjective matches a sense of the word meaning slim.

clue.text: European city in Antwerp or Toulouse

indicators.note: the answer is said to be inside the following words, sitting across their boundaries

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first city, the little word, and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Choosing between two European cities, one Belgian and one French, for a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Porto is the Portuguese name of the second city of Portugal, which English speakers often call Oporto.

clue.text: Charitable brand

definitions.meaning: first meaning: generous and considerate to others
second meaning: a type or sort of thing

explanation.surface: A company name chosen for a charity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for benevolent people and a noun for a sort or variety, as a brand is.

clue.text: Number in yours truly's street

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, so this is the possessive of me
a way is a road or street

explanation.surface: A house number on the speaker's own road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a house number, but it is a song, the one Frank Sinatra made famous.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song or musical piece, and this is a famous Sinatra hit.

clue.text: Enduring brew

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sturdy, resolute and long-lasting
second meaning: a dark, strong beer

explanation.surface: A beer that keeps well over time.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means strong and determined, as in a stout defence, and the noun is a dark beer such as Guinness.

clue.text: Good speller? Just gory method, unfortunately

parts.note: just and fair are synonyms

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome is a mishap, suggesting the preceding words have gone wrong and come out jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who spells words correctly is disappointed by a bloody technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good speller' suggests a person who spells words correctly; here the spell is magic, cast by a kind figure from fairy tales.
explanation.definitionFit: In fairy tales such as Cinderella this benevolent figure casts magic spells, so she is literally a good caster of spells.

clue.text: Republican visiting a state — this one?

definitions.text: Republican visiting a state — this one?

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so this piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a, taken as written, then the Midwestern state
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A Republican politician tours one of the American states.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a Republican could well be found in this state, which sits next door to Kansas.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkansas is a southern US state, a Republican stronghold, matching the hint of a state visited by a party member.

clue.text: Keep food for sandwiches

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one's livelihood, the basic means of support
second meaning: the literal ingredients of a basic sandwich

explanation.surface: Storing the ingredients for making packed lunches.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning one's keep is earning a living, and the phrase is an idiom for one's basic livelihood or main source of income.

clue.text: Male on the farm and servant run amok

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: A farm animal and a household servant go wild together.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently and wildly out of control, the same as the idiom from Malay.

clue.text: Vehicle for selling pictures?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an unpowered wheeled vehicle towed behind a car
second meaning: a short preview advertising a forthcoming film

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pictures' means films, as in going to the pictures; the question mark flags the playful sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a towed wagon and also a short promotional clip shown to market a new movie.

clue.text: Quiet performance mainly in movement, eerie initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word in the run before it

parts.note: the leading letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A silent show carried out mostly through gesture, with a spooky feel at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A mime is a silent piece of theatre performed through gesture and movement with no speech.

clue.text: Rare shot taken in pyjamas, sexy

indicators.note: the answer is held within the following words, straddling their boundary

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An unusual photograph of someone wearing alluring nightwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests a photo, but this is a billiards stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A massé is an uncommon billiards stroke made with a near-vertical cue to make the ball swerve sharply.

clue.text: Boot in source of water, soggy in the end

parts.note: a well is a source of water

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A boot left standing in a spring of water ends up soaked through.
explanation.walkthrough: A welly, short for wellington, is the British name for a rubber rain boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A welly is a waterproof rubber boot, the colloquial British shortening of wellington boot.

clue.text: Rubbish article I'm leaving

parts.note: tat is cheap, worthless stuff
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone storms out in disgust at a worthless newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta-ta is an informal British way of saying goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is a casual farewell, the sort of thing said when departing, so it stands for a parting remark.

clue.text: Stop advertisement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stopper or bung for a hole
second meaning: a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt a commercial.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a bung that seals a hole and also informal promotion of a product given in passing.

clue.text: Fund set up for ring

indicators.note: in a down clue being set up means raised from bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: a pool is a shared fund of money

explanation.surface: A fund established to buy a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop is a circular shape formed by a curve closing on itself, much like a ring.

clue.text: Clear something viscous that's blocked crack

indicators.note: something blocking a gap fills it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a slit is a narrow crack
tar is a thick sticky liquid

explanation.surface: Clearing away a sticky substance that has plugged up a crack.
explanation.definitionFit: A night sky lit by stars is one without cloud, so the adjective describes cloudless conditions.

clue.text: Pasta: large helping beyond comprehension, ultimately

indicators.note: one piece placed beyond another comes after it in the answer
ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of the word
oodles means a large quantity

explanation.surface: A big plate of pasta that is somehow impossible to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles are long thin strips of pasta, so they are an example of the general food category.

clue.text: Fire is green, breaking out orange finally

indicators.note: breaking out suggests things bursting apart, so the letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: letters to rearrange, taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of the colour

explanation.surface: A strange blaze burns green rather than orange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like a noun for flames, but here it is the verb meaning to fire up.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to stir them into action, so as a verb it means to invigorate or stimulate.

clue.text: Churchgoers not wholly in European city

indicators.note: not wholly present means incomplete, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a parish is the congregation of a local church

explanation.surface: Not all the faithful attend services in a continental city.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital of France and so is a city on the European continent.
